newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's industrial index hits new life high.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's industrial index hits new life high.

text.p: South Africa's industrial index on Thursday hit a new life high of 8,754.5 points surpassing the previous high seen on January 25, 1996, when the index was at 8,752.9 points.

The index gained 84.6 points, or 0.98 percent on positive sentiment from a lower than expected May consumer price inflation figure and the announcement of details on latest foreign exchange controls relaxation, dealers said.

South African financial authorities on Wednesday said that private individuals would each be allowed to invest 200,000 rand offshore from July 1, in a move which forms part of the country's phased removal of exchange controls.

The limit, above market expectations of 160,000 rand, answered one of two uncertainties that have plagued the market in recent weeks -- the other being what amount of foreign exchange will leave the country post July 1.
May inflation data released on Wednesday showed a lower-than-expected 9.5 percent annual rise, fuelling hopes of a cut in interest rates later this year.
